program_name: Ohio Opportunity Zone Tax Credit
description: Nonrefundable Ohio income tax credit of 10% of an investment in an Ohio Qualified Opportunity Fund that invests in Ohio Opportunity Zone projects (ORC 122.84); awarded in application rounds.
notes: FY2026-27 budget (HB 96) doubled the allocation to $50M and removed automatic funding after FY2027. Separate from the federal OZ 2.0 nomination process.

program_name: Ohio conformity to federal Opportunity Zone treatment
description: Ohio's income tax starts from federal adjusted gross income, so federal QOF gain deferral generally flows through; confirm current conformity with the Ohio Department of Taxation.
notes: Not confirmed against an Ohio Department of Taxation publication for this seed. Verify before relying.

program_name: Ohio New Markets Tax Credit Program
description: State tax credits (39% of the investment, claimed over seven years) allocated to CDEs for qualified low-income community investments in Ohio; up to $10M of allocation a year.
notes: Round 15 applications were due March 9, 2026. Pairs with the federal NMTC tract test shown in this report.

program_name: Ohio Job Creation Tax Credit (JCTC)
description: Refundable, performance-based credit equal to a percentage of new state income tax withholding from new full-time jobs; approved by the Ohio Tax Credit Authority before the project commitment.
notes: Apply before committing to the project. Rates and terms are set per project.

program_name: Ohio State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI)
description: Ohio Department of Development administers Ohio's SSBCI funds: Collateral Enhancement Program 2.0, CDFI Loan Participation Program, Ohio Venture Fund and Early Stage Focus Fund.
notes: Loan programs run through participating lenders and CDFIs.

program_name: North Carolina treatment of federal Opportunity Zone deferral
description: Secondary sources report that North Carolina does not follow the federal QOF gain deferral and exclusion, so the deferred gain is added back for NC tax; confirm with the NC Department of Revenue.
notes: Reported by practitioner sources, not confirmed against an NCDOR publication for this seed. Verify before relying.

program_name: North Carolina Opportunity Zones (NC Commerce)
description: NC Commerce runs the state's federal Opportunity Zone nominations (up to 202 tracts for the 2027 round) and publishes North Carolina OZ data and tools.
notes: Information resource; no separate state OZ credit identified.

program_name: Job Development Investment Grant (JDIG) and One North Carolina Fund
description: Discretionary, performance-based cash grants from NC Commerce for new and expanding employers. JDIG pays out of new withholding from created jobs; One NC requires a local government match.
notes: Competitive and negotiated per project, usually for larger job-creation projects.

program_name: North Carolina State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI)
description: NC Department of Commerce is the implementing agency; the NC Rural Center administers the loan participation, capital access and related SSBCI programs on its behalf (up to $201.9M allocation).
notes: The link is the Rural Center's SSBCI page (technical assistance). Allocation announced July 29, 2022 by NC Commerce.

program_name: Georgia State Opportunity Zone Job Tax Credit
description: Up to $3,500 per net new full-time job per year for five years (minimum two jobs) for businesses in areas the Georgia DCA designates as state Opportunity Zones; offsets income tax and withholding.
notes: Georgia's state-designated Opportunity Zones are a different map from federal Qualified Opportunity Zones. Needs DCA certification before claiming.

program_name: Georgia Job Tax Credit
description: Statewide job tax credit whose per-job amount and job threshold depend on the county's tier (tier 1 is most distressed); claimed on Form IT-CA.
notes: Link is DCA's program fact sheet (updated July 2025). Check the current county tier for the address.

program_name: Georgia treatment of federal Opportunity Zone deferral
description: Georgia conforms to the Internal Revenue Code as of a fixed date set by annual legislation; confirm with the Georgia Department of Revenue whether QOF deferral and the 2025 federal changes apply.
notes: Conformity status not determined for this seed. Verify before relying.

program_name: Georgia State Small Business Credit Initiative (SSBCI)
description: Georgia DCA administers SSBCI 2.0 (about $199.6M): Loan Participation, Small Business Credit Guarantee, CDFI, Venture Capital and Equity Direct programs.
notes: Small businesses apply through participating lenders.

program_name: Texas Opportunity Zones (Office of the Governor)
description: The Governor's office manages Texas's federal Opportunity Zone nominations and information. Texas has no personal income tax, so there is no state income tax deferral issue for individuals.
notes: The franchise (margin) tax follows its own fixed IRC conformity date. Confirm with the Comptroller how deferred gain is treated.

program_name: Texas Enterprise Zone Program (EZP)
description: State sales and use tax refunds for projects in economically distressed areas, tied to capital investment and jobs; the local community must nominate the company. Applications are due quarterly.
notes: Maximum refunds depend on the project designation level. Check the current table on the page.

program_name: Texas Enterprise Fund (TEF)
description: Performance-based deal-closing cash grant for projects with significant job creation and capital investment where a Texas site competes with an out-of-state option.
notes: Link is the Governor's incentives overview, which covers TEF. Competitive and negotiated.

program_name: Jobs, Energy, Technology and Innovation Act (JETI, Tax Code Ch. 403)
description: School district M&O property tax value limitation for large eligible projects, administered by the Texas Comptroller. In effect Jan 1, 2024 through Dec 31, 2033.
notes: Aimed at large manufacturing, energy and similar projects. Some sources describe extra benefits in Opportunity Zones; verify against the Comptroller's rules.

program_name: Texas Small Business Credit Initiative (TSBCI)
description: Texas's SSBCI programs, a Capital Access Program and a Loan Guarantee Program run through participating lenders, administered by the Texas Economic Development & Tourism Office in the Office of the Governor.
notes: Businesses with 499 or fewer employees. Ask a participating lender.

program_name: California nonconformity to federal Opportunity Zone treatment
description: California does not conform to the federal deferral or exclusion for gains invested in Qualified Opportunity Funds (IRC 1400Z-1/1400Z-2) or to the 2025 OBBBA changes, per the Franchise Tax Board.
notes: For California purposes the gain is generally taxed in the year of sale. Federal OZ benefits do not reduce California tax.

program_name: California Competes Tax Credit (GO-Biz)
description: Negotiated, nonrefundable income tax credit for businesses that commit to hiring and investment milestones in California; awarded in three application periods each fiscal year.
notes: FY2026-27 windows: Jul 20-Aug 10, 2026; Jan 4-25, 2027; Mar 1-15, 2027. Six-year carryover; recapture if milestones are missed.

program_name: California New Employment Credit (FTB)
description: Credit for hiring qualified full-time employees who work in a designated geographic area (census-tract based, redrawn Jan 1, 2025); employers must get a reservation for each employee.
notes: FTB says the credit is available only for taxable years beginning before Jan 1, 2026. Check whether it has been extended before using it.

program_name: California SSBCI: IBank Small Business Loan Guarantee Program
description: California IBank (part of GO-Biz) uses SSBCI funds mainly for its Small Business Loan Guarantee Program through participating lenders; CalCAP at the State Treasurer's office runs the other SSBCI programs.
notes: Check the current policy manual for loan and guarantee limits.
